title: Simulating the Mechanics of Lens Accommodation via a Manual Lens Stretcher
protocol: Obtain an eye sample from local slaughterhouse or tissue bank.
Cut and remove all excess tissue surrounding the sclera using disinfected surgical scissors and forceps.
Make a small incision along the side of the eye 3 mm away from the cornea using a razor blade.
Carefully cut further along the incision around the circumference of the eye using scissors, avoiding puncturing the lens.
Remove the posterior tissue of the eye using forceps.
Isolate the lens, zonules, ciliary body, and attached vitreous with forceps.
Remove excess vitreous to allow the lens to lay flat on the MLS.
Insert the 10 mm shoe bottoms and the corresponding shoe tops into the bottom plate of the MLS so there remains a 5 mm gap between the back wall of the shoe indent and the shoe itself.
Align the top and bottom plates, snapping the plates together; the device is now in the unstretched position.
Insert the plates into the plate case and the stopper screw into the hole located on the side of the bottom plate.
Insert the plate case into the base and place the wrench into the aligned indents.
Twist the wrench clockwise until it reaches the stopping screw to contract the shoes, and twist back counter-clockwise to return the shoes to the original unstretched position.
Insert the 10 mm shoe bottoms into the bottom plate in the MLS so that a 5 mm gap between remains the back wall of the shoe indent and the shoe itself.
Using curved forceps, place the extracted lens face up on the middle of the bottom plate so that the shoes are supporting the lens over the central hole.
Snap the corresponding top of the shoes into place, clipping only the zonules and the vitreous.
Visually ensure that the lens stays as centered as possible on the bottom plate.
Place an imaging system directly above the apparatus in order to capture videos and pictures of the stretching process.
Include a ruler in the frame of the picture to accurately size and scale images in post-processing.
Rotate the wrench in the clockwise direction to stretch the lens.
Photograph the stretched lens.
Rotate the wrench in the counter-clockwise direction to restore the sample to its resting state.
Photograph the final resting state of the lens.
Upload the image to ImageJ.
Select at least 40 points around the circumference of the lens using the "point" feature.
Use the "Analyze" → "Measure" option to yield the location of each selected point.
Fit the location points using software (e.g., MATLAB) to yield a radius and chi-square of the fit.
Convert the pixel radius and error into metrics using the photographed ruler.
Perform a paired two-tailed t-test to compare an individual lens before and after stretching from the MLS.
